𝗧𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗪𝗲𝗲𝗸𝗱𝗮𝘆'𝘀 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀
 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲: 𝗥𝘀 𝟮𝟱𝟬𝟬𝟬𝟬 - 𝗥𝘀 𝟯𝟱𝟬𝟬𝟬𝟬 (𝗶𝗲 𝗜𝗡𝗥 𝟮.𝟱-𝟯.𝟱 𝗟𝗣𝗔)
 Experience: 1+ yrs
 Location: Delhi

 As a Reparing and Testing Engineer, you will be responsible for diagnosing, repairing, and testing industrial electrical equipment and systems to ensure optimal performance and reliability. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot complex electrical wiring, PLC, HMI, and drive issues, implementing effective solutions that minimize downtime. Your role will involve detailed analysis of faults through advanced diagnostic tools, executing corrective actions, and validating system functionality against project specifications. You will also contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by documenting repair procedures, providing technical feedback, and maintaining up-to-date knowledge of industry standards and emerging technologies.

 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀
 • Diagnose and troubleshoot electrical wiring, PLC, HMI, and drive systems in industrial settings.
 • Conduct comprehensive testing of repaired equipment to verify performance and safety standards.
 • Prepare accurate fault reports and recommend preventive maintenance activities.
 • Collaborate with engineering and production teams to resolve complex technical issues.
 • Assist in the installation and commissioning of new electrical and automation systems.
 • Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation of repair and testing procedures.
 • Ensure compliance with electrical codes, safety regulations, and quality standards.
 • Provide technical support and training to junior technicians and site personnel.
 • Coordinate with vendors for spare part procurement and specification verification.
 • Contribute to continuous improvement projects aimed at enhancing system reliability.

 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗠𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗮 𝗚𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁 𝗙𝗶𝘁
 • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related field.
 • 1+ year of hands‑on experience in electrical repair and testing in a manufacturing or automation environment.
 • Proficient knowledge of PLC programming and HMI configuration.
 • Strong understanding of motor drives and variable frequency drives (VFDs).
 • Familiarity with PLC diagnostic tools and oscilloscope usage.
 • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical manuals.
 • Excellent problem‑solving skills and a methodical approach to troubleshooting.
 • Strong communication skills and the ability to document findings clearly.
 • Proactive attitude towards continuous learning and applying new technologies.
 • Commitment to maintaining a safe and compliant work environment.
